newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Large-cap shares seen rebounding on Seoul bourse.
newsitem.headline: Large-cap shares seen rebounding on Seoul bourse.

text.p: Large-capitalised shares are expected to rebound on Tuesday following recent sharp falls but brokers said the market in general needed to consolidate more.
"Large-capitalised shares are likely to try to stage a technical rebound," said Kim Dae-hee at LG Securities. "But the market will turn around after falling to the 740 level."
Brokers said banking shares would fluctuate in anticipation of a scheduled government announcement on individual shareholding ceiling in banks.
The composite stock index closed on Monday at 753.05, down 7.35 points.

In a meeting with finance minister Kang Kyong-shik on Monday, Kia Group Chairman Kim Sun-hong asked the minister to persuade merchant banks to maintain credit to the nation's eighth-largest chaebol. He also said Kia affiliates would seek restructuring to improve their financial status.
Kia Group shares recently have taken a beating on rumours of financial troubles in the group.
The finance and economy ministry said it would unveil government's stance this week on the ownership ceiling in domestic banks.
